en: The Banaue Rice Terraces act as giant inclined planes, reducing the force needed for farmers to carry heavy harvests up the mountain.
Jeepney tires have deep treads to increase friction and prevent skidding on wet roads during the Philippine rainy season.
The strong gravitational pull of the moon causes the high and low tides observed daily in Manila Bay.
Black sand beaches in Ilocos contain magnetite, a magnetic iron ore that can be attracted by a simple bar magnet.
The Tiwi Geothermal Power Plant in Albay converts heat energy from underground volcanic steam into electrical energy for the Luzon grid.
Bioluminescent fireflies in Loboc, Bohol, produce visible light energy through a chemical reaction inside their abdomens.
Visitors hear a distinct echo inside the Puerto Princesa Underground River because sound waves bounce off the hard limestone cave walls.
Filipino cooks use the conduction of heat to fry crispy pata, transferring thermal energy directly from the hot pan to the meat.
A traditional vinta boat in Zamboanga possesses kinetic energy because of its forward motion across the waves of the Sulu Sea.
A street vendor uses a wooden lever to weigh bananas on a traditional hanging scale called a timbangan.
The massive scrap cranes at the Manila International Container Port use electromagnets to lift and drop heavy steel shipping containers.
A ripe carabao mango hanging high on a tree branch stores gravitational potential energy due to its elevated position.
